purpose: Teach: たべ/横たわっ/のる/盗み/名乗り/注が/申し述べ/惜しみ

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、ご飯はちゃんとたべましょうね
lines.en: Sho, eat your rice properly, won't you.
lines.style: Gentle, matter-of-fact reminder. Even tone, no urgency. The kind of instruction given without thinking—maternal routine.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、お祖父ちゃんがソファに横たわって眠ってらしたよ
lines.en: Mom, Grandpa was lying down sleeping on the sofa.
lines.style: Quiet, factual observation. Slight pause before speaking, as if still processing what he saw. No judgment—just reporting what is.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、自転車にのる時は気を付けてね
lines.en: Sho, be careful when you ride your bike.
lines.style: Attentive but brief. Steady, protective tone without fussing. The kind of care that doesn't draw attention to itself.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お祖父ちゃんとお話で笑いの盗みっこしたよ
lines.en: Mom, I played a game with Grandpa where we stole each other's laughs.
lines.style: Bright and eager. Quick delivery, genuinely delighted. The joy in his voice is simple and unguarded. Slight lilt at the end.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お祖父ちゃんが昔のお名前を名乗りで紹介して下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, Grandpa introduced himself by his old name, you know.
lines.style: Reflective, noticing. Soft, thoughtful tone. She's turning something over in her mind—what it means that he did this.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんがお茶を注がれるのを見たよ
lines.en: Mom, I watched Dad pour the tea.
lines.style: Simple and present. Not seeking praise—just sharing what he noticed. Spoken with the quiet certainty of someone who takes in details others miss.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お祖父ちゃんがご感想を申し述べて下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, Grandpa shared his thoughts with us.
lines.style: Warm, respectful. Calm delivery. A moment of subtle pride—in her son for listening, in her father for offering his words.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お祖父ちゃんがおやつを惜しみなくくれたよ
lines.en: Mom, Grandpa gave me snacks without holding back.
lines.style: Content and warm. A gentle smile in the voice. Sho is saying this with simple gratitude—the kind a child has when generosity feels like love.
